recommendation: Keep the empty audit commit as-is. No follow-up is needed for FHIR-37001 unless OO later changes the Task.code binding policy or the Task.restriction invariant.
issue_request: FHIR-37001 was an Applied/Persuasive FHIR-core Task change request asking OO to change Task.code from an example binding to an extensible binding so the existing task-code values, especially 'fulfill', can support the Task.restriction invariant introduced by FHIR-31900.
initial_application: The change was already applied in current source. Git history contains FHIR-37001 commits from 2025-03-09, and current blame attributes the Task.code binding strength line to 50d02c76bd866915254d40e1203e6939514cd234, which changed source/task/structuredefinition-Task.xml from example to extensible.
additional_context: source/fhir.ini actively lists task=Task under [resources], so source/task/structuredefinition-Task.xml is in current build scope. The current Task source still has the Task.restriction invariant requiring Task.code 'fulfill' from http://hl7.org/fhir/CodeSystem/task-code, and OO minutes from 2025-02-07 record the FHIR-37001 motion and 8-0-2 vote. Searches found no later FHIR-core decision reversing the extensible binding.
reconciliation: No source files were changed. The authoritative Task StructureDefinition already has strength="extensible" for Task.code and points to http://hl7.org/fhir/ValueSet/task-code, whose compose includes http://hl7.org/fhir/CodeSystem/task-code with the 'fulfill' code.

related_jiras.note: Published Task.restriction clarification added the invariant that depends on Task.code 'fulfill', motivating the binding-strength change audited for FHIR-37001.
